Its reviewer re-ran everything independently including three feature-deletion sabotages that each turned the gate red, a 2,000-dev scale build at 8,953 pages in 35 seconds, and a full-tree grep accounting for all 123 simonw hits as signal citations of his public writing with ZERO occurrences of /cerebro/dev/simonw anywhere. Guarded, COUNTED not swallowed, because a bare except-pass would rebuild the exact hole that let e03 print healthy:true through 273 rate-limit errors. Three tests, each proved load-bearing by removing the guard and watching them fail. Also token_check.py was outside the no-composite sweep on the argument that it holds no person-level data, which is precisely the exemption the sweep's own comment warns is where the next one hides. e07: a real login literal was compiled into server/chunks/223.js via an error message naming fixtures/devs/simonw.md, in the OPT-OUT build too, so it now cites the directory; and the gate's two whole-file sweeps used bare .includes(login) which reddens on a login that is a substring of another published login, fail-closed but a launch gate that can go red for the wrong person is one somebody eventually argues with, now bounded to the GitHub login class and unit-checked so samsmith no longer matches sam. Gate re-run after both: --login simonw EXIT=0 with all five treatment surfaces ABSENT, --login nobodyhere EXIT=1. THE PROGRAMME NOW STOPS AND THE REASON IS NOT A DEFECT. e08 is LAUNCH: merge the stack and publish /cerebro/devs. That publishes pages about 26 NAMED REAL PEOPLE whose verdicts are ALL agent-recorded, 0 owner-signed, and the ATC directive is explicit that nothing gets stamped reviewed_by owner until Stevie has actually looked. His standing 'do not wait for human' authority covers decisions I can take with codex or a recommended option; it does not cover deciding, on his behalf, to publish judgements about real people in his name. That is the one gate the charter, the ATC correction and the CI test I added all point at the same way.
